To find the weight of the Mastiff, we will determine the weight of each dog in the line step by step, based on the relationships provided in the problem.

**Step 1: Determine the weight of the Affenpinscher.**
The problem states that the first dog, the Affenpinscher, weighed 10 pounds.
$$ \text{Weight of Affenpinscher} = 10 \text{ pounds} $$

**Step 2: Determine the weight of the Dachshund.**
The Dachshund sat next to the Affenpinscher and weighed twice as much as the Affenpinscher.
$$ \text{Weight of Dachshund} = 2 \times \text{Weight of Affenpinscher} $$
$$ \text{Weight of Dachshund} = 2 \times 10 = 20 \text{ pounds} $$

**Step 3: Determine the weight of the Papillon.**
The Papillon sat next to the Dachshund and weighed one-fourth as much as the Dachshund.
$$ \text{Weight of Papillon} = \frac{1}{4} \times \text{Weight of Dachshund} $$
$$ \text{Weight of Papillon} = \frac{1}{4} \times 20 = 5 \text{ pounds} $$

**Step 4: Determine the weight of the Mastiff.**
The Mastiff sat at the end of the line and weighed 44 times the weight of the Papillon.
$$ \text{Weight of Mastiff} = 44 \times \text{Weight of Papillon} $$
$$ \text{Weight of Mastiff} = 44 \times 5 $$

Calculating the product:
$$ 44 \times 5 = 220 $$

So, the Mastiff weighed 220 pounds.

Final answer: 220
